exposure: Number of previous spontaneous abortions (two vs. three or more)
outcome: Recurrent loss (spontaneous abortion in the current pregnancy)
cohort: Ninety-five pregnant women with two or more previous spontaneous abortions were prospectively followed at a tertiary care center in South India.
finding: Women with three or more prior spontaneous abortions had significantly higher odds of adverse obstetric outcomes (cesarean delivery, recurrent loss, preterm birth) and neonatal outcomes (low birth weight, low Apgar scores) compared to those with two prior losses.
mod_finding: Women with three or more prior spontaneous abortions had higher odds of cesarean delivery (OR = 2.8; 95% CI = 1.1-7.5) compared with those with two losses.
